gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-elbasan: Noto Sans Elbasan reads large and open, with terminals that never pinch shut. Visitor is the show-off, crossbars as thick as its stems and built for loud moments, while the body font does the patient, steady work of carrying lowercase text.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-elymaic: Gaping mouths on the e and stubby ascenders over fat bowls give Visitor its pixel-era look. Noto Sans Elymaic then reads smoothly, apertures wide open.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-ethiopic: Chunky, retro and a bit rebellious, Visitor draws with a marker-nib line that ignores direction, so every letter feels stamped on. It earns its keep big and short.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-georgian: Retro pixel charm, with a t whose crossbar and stem share one width. Noto Sans Georgian takes over for the reading, its sans-serif curves open throughout while Visitor handles the attention-grabbing.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-glagolit: Noto Sans Glagolitic is round, sturdy and friendly at small sizes. Visitor adds its plain constant-width lines and gaping e on top, a nostalgic jolt that the body text calmly absorbs.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-gothic: Noto Sans Gothic reads with big, bead-like counters and round forms like open parentheses. Visitor, with strokes like thread stitched along a path, brings the retro digital flavor; the body font brings the ease.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-grantha: Visitor runs a single flat line weight through every glyph, with short ascenders perched above big bowls. Give Noto Sans Grantha the generous size, since its small, tall letters need it.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-gujarati: Noto Sans Gujarati reads with curved strokes that stop before turning inward, leaving generous counters in a, e and s. Visitor, with joints that never thin or bulge, grabs attention; the body simply carries the words.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-gunjala-: Blocky, glowing and nostalgic, Visitor keeps a monoweight skeleton under its gaping e. Noto Sans Gunjala Gondi brings terminals cut back to leave a big gap.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-gurmukhi: Pixel-era punch from a steady, marker-like line, with short ascenders over big bowls. Noto Sans Gurmukhi sends its terminals outward like tongs, so the heading shouts and the text keeps talking.
